structure.title: Preface
structure.summary: The text is a covering letter from JSW Steel Limited to stock exchanges (NSE and BSE) regarding the submission of its Integrated Annual Report for FY 2024-25, which includes the Notice of the 31st Annual General Meeting and the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report, pursuant to SEBI LODR Regulation 34. The report is sent electronically to members with registered email addresses, and a letter with the website link is sent to others. The letter also includes a tribute to the founder, O.P. Jindal, and highlights JSW Steel's position as India's largest steelmaker, with key capacity figures and employee count. The accompanying Integrated Report contents cover introduction, organizational overview, strategy, sustainability, governance, management discussion and analysis, statutory reports, financial statements, and AGM notice.

structure.title: ABOUT THE REPORT
structure.summary: JSW Steel's 8th Integrated Annual Report for FY 2024-25 transparently communicates value creation over short, medium, and long term, covering capacity, capabilities, operating context, strategy, risk management, financial and non-financial performance, and corporate governance. It details reporting cycle (April 2024-March 2025), frameworks (IR, UN SDGs, GHG Protocol, NGRBC, GRI, worldsteel, UNGC, CDP, BRSR), financial reporting standards (Companies Act, Ind AS, SEBI LODR, Secretarial Standards), and scope/boundary for strategic, financial, and non-financial disclosures across listed entities. It includes precautionary principle, value creation approach, responsibility statement, assurance by Bureau Veritas and SRBC & Co. LLP, and forward-looking statements disclaimer.

structure.title: Highest ever production and sales
structure.summary: The text highlights JSW Steel's record production and sales, including crude steel production of 27.79 MnT (up 5.1%), steel sales of 26.45 MnT (up 6.7%), and value-added product sales of 15.40 MnT. Responsible growth initiatives feature a 30% reduction in CO2 emission intensity, specific energy consumption of 5.48 Gcal/tcs, 99.98% waste utilization, over 4.5 lakh safety observations, 26,355+ safety inspections, 7,750 e-learning modules, ₹363 crore CSR spend, 30 lakh beneficiaries, and 11 projects in art and culture. It also notes global validation as a worldsteel Sustainability Champion 2025 and an ESG score, and describes JSW Steel's alignment with India's Viksit Bharat @2047 roadmap through capacity expansion, innovation, green steel, livelihoods, education, healthcare, and social justice.

structure.title: Partnering India's infrastructure push

It also covers steel supply to energy projects including solar, wind, and thermal power plants. The document references sections on innovating to serve evolving needs, nurturing a future-ready workforce, harnessing digital technologies, and enriching life and livelihoods, all part of the Integrated Report 2024-25.

structure.title: JSW Steel Capacity Expansion and Innovation Strategy

It highlights near-term capacity projects and downstream expansion (13.5 MTPA) for infrastructure, automotive, renewable energy, and defence. The page also covers innovation to serve evolving needs, including VASP share (62%), branded sales (48%), and 100 new products/grades. It describes advanced steel solutions: AHSS for safety and lightweighting, electrical steel (CRNO/CRGO) for energy efficiency, and tinplate for sustainable packaging, including the acquisition of Thyssenkrupp's CRGO facility and setup of India's first end-to-end CRGO line.

structure.title: JSW Steel: Digital Transformation and Green Steel Future

structure.title: Workforce Development and Community Livelihood Initiatives
structure.summary: The page covers JSW Steel's workforce and community initiatives. It details nurturing a future-ready workforce through new hires, total permanent employees, training hours, and learning themes aligned with Industry 5.0. It highlights leadership development programs, DE&I efforts including women-run units and women engineer recruitment. key_items: 1 Value-accretive capacity expansion to address India’s growing steel demand

nodes.title: JSW Steel Chairman's Message on Growth, Resilience, and Innovation
key_items: Innovating to make steel more versatile
nodes.summary: The Chairman's message addresses shareholders on navigating global volatility, India's growth, and steel industry challenges like weak global demand and Chinese exports. JSW Steel is India's largest steelmaker with 34.2 MTPA capacity, targeting 50 MTPA by FY2030-31, and focuses on value-added capacities and competitive capex. It highlights US tariffs, trade barriers, and India's 12% safeguard duty, advocating for a long-term solution. India's steel consumption grew 11.5% y-o-y to 152 MnT, with government infrastructure push and manufacturing growth sustaining demand. JSW achieved record production and sales, with revenue of ₹1,68,824 crore and EBITDA of ₹22,904 crore. Capacity expansions at JVML and BPSL are ramping up. The company is innovating with value-added products (62% of sales), alloy steel, colour-coated steel, and CRGO electrical steel, including a JV with JFE Steel and a new integrated CRGO facility. R&D focuses on advanced grades and sustainability, highlighted by the launch of Magsure for solar applications.

structure.summary: The text covers India's automotive sector shift toward safer, cleaner mobility, driven by safety norms, fuel efficiency, and EVs, boosting demand for advanced high-strength steel, with the market projected to reach US$7,581.1 million by 2030 at 7.7% CAGR, and JSW Steel's investments in sustainable steel solutions. nodes.title: Steel Expansion Projects: Vijayanagar and Dolvi Updates
nodes.summary: The page provides key project updates on steel expansion at Vijayanagar and Dolvi. At Vijayanagar, the 5 MTPA integrated steel project is near completion, with a 4.5 MTPA blast furnace commissioned and operating above 90% capacity, a 3.3 MTPA Steel Melt Shop with one converter and both casters operational, and the second converter expected in Q2 FY 2025-26. Commercial production from the HSM unit began in March 2024, allied facilities are commissioned, and the Coke Oven project has three of four batteries commissioned. Blast Furnace 3 will be upgraded from 3 to 4.5 MTPA, increasing crude steel capacity to 19 MTPA, with commissioning in Q4 FY 2025-26. At Dolvi, the Phase III expansion from 10 to 15 MTPA includes a 4.8 MTPA blast furnace, 5 MTPA Steel Melt Shop, Hybrid Continuous Strip Mill, and a 250 MW captive power plant, with long lead equipment ordered and completion targeted for September 2027.

nodes.title: Independent Assurance Statement for JSW Steel Integrated Report 2024-25
nodes.summary: Bureau Veritas provides independent assurance for JSW Steel's sustainability disclosures in its Integrated Report for April 2024–March 2025. Reasonable assurance covers BRSR Core, while limited assurance covers BRSR nine principles and GRI-based IR; verification occurred December 2024–May 2025. The statement is intended solely for JSW Steel and its stakeholders, with liability limited to JSW Steel. Reporting criteria include the International <IR> Framework, GRI Standards, World Steel Association environmental indicators, GHG Protocol, and SEBI BRSR requirements. Assurance was conducted per ISAE 3000 (Revised) for reasonable assurance and ISAE 3410 for GHG, assessing relevance, completeness, materiality, reliability, neutrality, and understandability.

It details limited assurance for general and topic-specific disclosures (GRI 2, 3, 301-308, 401-418) including gap assessment and assurance statement completion, and reasonable assurance for BRSR Core topics (GHG, water, energy, waste, employee wellbeing, gender diversity, inclusive development, customer/supplier fairness, open-ness) and for all environmental topics at listed locations. The scope includes assessment of data compilation procedures, sample testing, verification, and suitability of backup data for IR and BRSR.

nodes.title: Limitations and Exclusions
nodes.summary: The text outlines limitations and exclusions of an assurance engagement. It also specifies that Scope-3 GHG emissions data (305-3) covers purchased goods and services (raw materials only), fuel- and energy-related activities, upstream transportation and distribution, business travel, employee commuting, downstream transportation and distribution, processing of sold products, and use of sold products.

nodes.title: The methodology adopted for Assurance
nodes.summary: Bureau Veritas's assurance methodology for JSW Steel's sustainability data includes tailored procedures to verify non-financial disclosures, risks, and internal strategy. The scope covers reporting framework adherence (GRI, BRSR, materiality, inclusivity, responsiveness), data integrity and systems (assumptions, data compilation, month-wise reliability), strategic alignment and stakeholder engagement (risk discussions, materiality assessment, strategy execution), verification and audit trail (site visits, claim reviews, audit trails), and governance and reporting quality (ESG policies, balanced representation, GHG emissions procedures). Conclusions affirm the Integrated Report and BRSR are proper, adequate, and reliable. Responsibilities, uncertainty, independence, competence, and restrictions on use are also addressed.

nodes.title: Reinforcing cost leadership through integrated manufacturing
nodes.summary: JSW Steel reinforces cost leadership through integrated manufacturing, efficient operations, strategically located plants, and advanced technologies. Its integrated operations span raw material processing to downstream value-added products, with strong logistics connectivity. Cost-reduction initiatives in FY 2024–25 included regional iron ore sourcing, optimized coking coal blends, increased PCI, and better utilization of blast furnace and coke oven gases. The company is implementing renewable energy plans, with power purchase agreements for 996 MW (Phase I) and 1,470 MW (Phase II) of wind and solar power. By FY 2026–27, a 30 MTPA slurry pipeline and 8 MTPA Odisha pellet plant will enhance logistics and raw material security. The company secured 23 iron ore and three coking coal mines in India, targeting 25% captive coking coal sourcing, and acquired international coal assets in Mozambique and Australia.

nodes.title: Value-added and special steel products

The company established J2ES, a 50:50 JV with JFE, which acquired Thyssenkrupp Electrical Steel India (renamed J2ESNPL) for ₹4,159 crore, gaining a 50,000 TPA GOES plant in Nashik. Digital focus areas span primary functions like mining, supply chain, manufacturing, sales, HR, and finance, plus additional areas such as safety, sustainability R&D, cultural transformation, and control towers, with anticipated impacts on sales, costs, assets, emissions, safety, and workforce. Green steel initiatives include a pilot green hydrogen project at Vijayanagar, preparation for EU CBAM and India's Net Zero 2070 target, and transfer of the Salav DRI unit to JSW Green Steel Limited for ₹2,233 crore, with plans to expand capacity from 0.9 to 4 MTPA in two phases.

XVIII. Investment in subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures
Investment in subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures are shown at cost or deemed cost applied on transition to Ind AS, less impairment, in accordance with the option available in Ind AS 27, ‘Separate Financial Statements’. Where the carrying amount of an investment in greater than its estimated recoverable amount, it is written down immediately to its recoverable amount and the difference is recognised in the Statement of Profit and Loss. On disposal of investment, the difference between the net disposal proceeds and the carrying amount is recognised in the Statement of Profit and Loss.

The material accounting policies section covers the statement of compliance, confirming preparation in accordance with Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) and Schedule III, and approval by the Board. It then details the basis of preparation and presentation, including historical cost basis, fair value measurement, fair value hierarchy levels (1, 2, 3), currency and rounding, and the classification of assets and liabilities as current or non-current based on the operating cycle and other criteria. nodes.title: III. Basis of consolidation�

It details consolidation procedures including combining like items, offsetting parent investment, eliminating intragroup transactions, attributing profit/loss and OCI to owners and non-controlling interests, and adjusting subsidiary accounting policies. It also covers business combinations using the acquisition method, including consideration measurement, identifiable assets/liabilities recognition, goodwill calculation, bargain purchases, non-controlling interests measurement, step acquisitions, provisional accounting, and common control transactions using pooling of interests. Additionally, it addresses investment property initial and subsequent measurement, depreciation, and derecognition; goodwill impairment testing and allocation to cash-generating units; and investments in associates and joint ventures using the equity method, including significant influence, joint control, loss recognition limits, and goodwill/impaired gain on acquisition.

nodes.title: Accounting Policies for Business Combinations, Investment Property, and Goodwill
nodes.summary: The page outlines accounting policies for business combinations, investment property, and goodwill. Business combinations use the acquisition method, covering consideration measurement, identifiable assets/liabilities recognition, goodwill calculation, bargain purchases, non-controlling interests, step acquisitions, provisional accounting, and common control transactions via pooling of interests. Investment property is initially at cost, subsequently at cost less depreciation/impairment, depreciated over 30 years, and derecognized on disposal with gains/losses in profit or loss. Goodwill is carried at cost less impairment, allocated to cash-generating units, tested annually for impairment, impairment loss not reversed, and included in disposal profit/loss. The policy for goodwill on associate/joint venture acquisitions is referenced.

nodes.title: VII. Investment in associates and joint ventures

nodes.title: Share-Based Payments and Taxes in Consolidated Financial Statements

nodes.title: XVI. Property, plant and equipment
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for property, plant and equipment (PPE), intangible assets, mining assets, impairment of non-financial assets, and inventories. For PPE, it details initial measurement at cost or deemed cost, cost components, subsequent expenditure, derecognition, capital work in progress, depreciation methods and useful lives (including different lives for Indian and foreign assets), and annual review of residual values. Intangible assets are measured at cost or fair value in a business combination, amortized over finite lives, with indefinite life assets tested for impairment. Mining assets include acquisition costs, exploration and evaluation, stripping costs, and site restoration provisions. Impairment of non-financial assets is assessed annually or when indicators exist, with recoverable amount as higher of fair value less costs to sell and value in use. Inventories are stated at lower of cost and net realizable value.

nodes.title: XX. Inventories

Financial instruments are initially at fair value and classified into amortised cost, FVTOCI, or FVTPL. Impairment uses expected credit loss models, with lifetime ECL for significant credit risk increases and 12-month ECL otherwise. The effective interest method is applied. Derivative and hedge accounting, segment reporting, and key estimation uncertainties are addressed. Commodity price risk, interest rate risk, and equity price risk are analyzed with sensitivities. Credit risk and liquidity risk management are detailed, including exposure limits and maturity tables.

nodes.title: XX. Inventories (intro)
nodes.summary: The text outlines accounting policies for inventories, provisions, and financial instruments. Net realisable value and provisions for slow-moving/obsolete items are explained. Provisions are recognized for present obligations, measured at best estimate, including onerous contracts. Financial instruments are initially measured at fair value, with classification into amortised cost, FVTOCI, or FVTPL based on business model and cash flow characteristics. nodes.title: Inventory Valuation, Provisions, and Financial Instruments Accounting Policies

nodes.title: d) Impairment of financial assets
nodes.summary: The text details the Group's impairment policy for financial assets under expected credit loss (ECL) model. It explains measuring loss allowance at lifetime ECL if credit risk increased significantly since initial recognition, otherwise at 12-month ECL, with reversion to 12-month if credit quality improves. It defines ECL as weighted average credit losses, credit loss as difference between contractual and expected cash flows discounted at original effective interest rate, and estimation considering all contractual terms. It describes assessing significant increase in credit risk by comparing default risk at reporting date versus initial recognition using reasonable supportable information. The ECL model applies to amortised cost assets, debt instruments at FVTOCI, lease receivables, trade receivables, other contractual rights, and financial guarantees not at FVTPL. For trade receivables under Ind AS 115, lifetime ECL is always used, with a provision matrix practical expedient incorporating historical loss experience and forward-looking information. For FVTOCI debt instruments, loss allowance is recognized in other comprehensive income without reducing carrying amount. Sensitivity analysis performed, and the Group expects recovery of carrying amounts based on current economic indicators.

nodes.title: F. Commodity price risk
nodes.summary: The text covers commodity price risk, detailing the Group's exposure to steel price fluctuations influenced by supply and demand, production costs, and economic conditions, and to raw material price fluctuations for iron ore, coking coal, ferro alloys, zinc, and scrap, purchased at market prices. nodes.title: G. Interest rate risk
nodes.summary: The text covers interest rate risk, defined as fluctuations in fair value or cash flows due to market interest rate changes. The Group is exposed through fixed and floating rate borrowings, primarily in rupees and US dollars, and uses interest rate swaps to hedge US dollar exposure. Risk is measured via cash flow sensitivity and managed by maintaining a mix of fixed and floating rate borrowings and swap contracts. A table shows fixed and floating borrowings as of March 31, 2025, and 2024. Sensitivity analysis indicates a 100 basis point change would impact profit by ₹605 crores (2025) and ₹495 crores (2024). nodes.title: Notice Items: Secretarial Auditor, Cost Auditor, and Independent Director Appointment
nodes.summary: The page begins with a notice about a Supreme Court order maintaining status quo pending a review petition and clarifies Explanatory Statement requirements. Item No. 4 details the appointment of M/s. S. Srinivasan & Co. as Secretarial Auditors for five years (FY 2025-26 to 2029-30) under SEBI Regulations, including their credentials, consent, remuneration of ₹10.80 lakhs, and Board recommendation for an Ordinary Resolution. Item No. 5 covers the re-appointment of M/s. Shome & Banerjee as Cost Auditor for FY 2025-26 at ₹23,00,000 remuneration, requiring member ratification via Ordinary Resolution. Item No. 6 addresses the appointment of Mr. Shyamal Mukherjee as an Additional Independent Director for five years (July 23, 2025 to July 22, 2030), including his qualifications, declarations of independence, consent, and Board recommendation for a Special Resolution. nodes.title: Item No. 7
nodes.summary: JSW Steel outlines its growth strategy with ₹61,863 crore capex over FY2025-26 to FY2027-28 for capacity expansion, digitalization, and efficiency projects, while pursuing M&A opportunities. It emphasizes the need to raise long-term resources via equity or convertible instruments to strengthen the balance sheet and optimize capital structure. A fresh enabling resolution is proposed to raise up to ₹7,000 crore each through non-convertible debentures with warrants and equity shares/convertible securities via QIP, with proceeds for capex, debt refinancing, or general corporate purposes. nodes.title: Item No. 8 to 21
nodes.summary: The text covers SEBI regulations on material related party transactions (RPTs), including thresholds (₹1,000 crores or 10% of turnover) and shareholder approval requirements, with exemptions for wholly owned subsidiaries. It details JSW Steel's compliance process, Audit Committee approval, and restrictions on related party voting for resolutions 8 to 21. It also discusses the Supreme Court judgment rejecting JSW Steel's resolution plan for Bhushan Power & Steel Ltd (BPSL), directing refunds and liquidation, and JSW Steel's evaluation of legal remedies while continuing consolidation of BPSL. Finally, it provides background on JSW Energy's power generation capacity and JSW Steel's steel plant capacities, explaining the rationale for procuring power from JSW Energy under long-term agreements due to unreliable state electricity supply and cost advantages, including specifics of job work and power purchase agreements.

nodes.title: Item No. 8

nodes.title: Item No. 9
key_items: Background, details and benefits of the transaction:
nodes.summary: This notice seeks shareholder approval for material related party transactions between JSW Steel Limited and JSW Jaigarh Port Limited (JSWJPL), a wholly owned subsidiary of JSW Infrastructure Limited. The transactions involve cargo handling, operation and maintenance of raw material handling systems, transportation via mini bulk carriers, coal blending, port disbursement account charges, sale of land, and other business-related transactions. The total proposed value is ₹1,577 crores, ₹1,560 crores, and ₹2,268 crores for FY 2025-26, 2026-27, and 2027-28, respectively, aggregating to ₹5,405 crores, plus ₹5,707 crores for the remaining period of agreements. The transactions exceed the ₹1,000 crore materiality threshold, necessitating shareholder approval. The notice details the background, benefits, justification, pricing methodology, and relevant disclosures under SEBI regulations, including information about the related party, transaction values, and past transactions. The Board recommends the resolution.

nodes.title: Item No. 10
key_items: Background, details and benefits of the transaction:

It details BMM's background, JSWPL's 58.47% acquisition, and BMM's new 0.88 MTPA integrated steel plant. Proposed RPTs include JSW Steel purchasing TMT bars, billets, DRI, and coal from BMM; selling coal, iron ore, and steel products to BMM; and other business transactions. Benefits include market share growth, capacity utilization, cost optimization, and raw material security. The text also covers transaction details, pricing methodology, regulatory compliance, and board recommendations.

nodes.title: Item No. 11

It also includes regulatory disclosures such as JSL's financials, pricing methodology, board and audit committee approvals, and director interest.

nodes.title: Item No. 12

nodes.title: Item No. 13

The text details the background, justification, economic benefits, loan terms, pricing methodology, and prior approvals from the Audit Committee and Board. nodes.title: Item No. 15

nodes.title: Item No. 17

nodes.summary: This notice seeks shareholder approval for related party transactions (RPTs) between JSW Steel USA Ohio Inc. (JSW Ohio), a wholly owned subsidiary of JSW Steel Limited, and Jindal Tubular USA LLC (Jindal Tubular), a related party under SEBI regulations. JSW Ohio is undertaking a USD 145 million capex project to install Vacuum Tank Degassing and Caster Dynamic Soft Reduction at its Mingo Junction, Ohio facility, enabling production of value-added API-grade hot rolled coils (HRC) for markets including oil and gas. The proposed RPTs involve JSW Ohio supplying API-grade HRC to Jindal Tubular, with estimated annual values of USD 127 million for FY 2025-26, FY 2026-27, and FY 2027-28, totaling USD 381 million, exceeding materiality thresholds. The notice details the background, benefits, economic rationale, transaction specifics, and related party information, including Jindal Tubular's ownership and financials. It also notes interim supply arrangements for FY 2025-26 via slab sourcing and conversion by ATI, and confirms Audit Committee and Board approvals. The resolution is recommended for shareholder approval.

For each, it covers name, DIN, date of birth/age, date of first appointment, qualifications, brief resume and expertise, terms of appointment, remuneration, relationship with other directors/KMP, board meeting attendance, other directorships, committee memberships, shareholding, and skills matching. Rathore is Wholetime Director & COO with 37 years in steel; Mukherjee is former PwC Chairman and proposed Non-Executive Independent Director. Includes regulatory references and notes on committee consideration.

structure.summary: This document provides corporate information for JSW Steel, including its board of directors, key management, auditors, bankers, registered office, registrar, and works locations. It then presents an overview of JSW Steel as the flagship of the US$23 billion JSW Group, detailing its consolidated and domestic crude steel capacities, growth plans, and its largest plant in Vijayanagar. The overview highlights research and innovation, strategic collaboration with JFE Steel, and recognition for business and sustainability practices, including Responsible Steel certification and sustainability indices. It outlines sustainability targets such as CO2 reduction, net neutrality by 2050, renewable energy by 2030, biodiversity, and water management. Finally, it mentions workplace certifications and rankings.
